name: Society Pass Incorporated

profile.description: Society Pass is a Southeast Asia-focused digital ecosystem company operating across Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Thailand in digital marketing, lifestyle, beauty, travel, and food & beverage verticals. The company claims 3.3 million registered users and 205,000 registered merchants. On May 12, 2026, Society Pass and its SoPa subsidiary filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy (Houston, Case No. 26-90525), and Nasdaq moved to delist shares on May 21, 2026, suspending trading despite the company's planned appeal. Market cap has collapsed to approximately $1M. The most recent earnings (March 2026) showed revenue of $2.05M and EPS of -$0.15, with TTM revenue of $7.1M and net losses of -$10.2M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): Society Pass has failed to establish a viable business model in five years of operation. Revenue declined 18% YoY in the most recently reported quarter, the company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2026, and Nasdaq initiated delisting proceedings [1][2]. No successful product launches, market pivots, or business model transformations were identified — the multi-vertical digital platform strategy across five Southeast Asian countries spread resources too thin without achieving scale in any category. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI product deployment, AI-driven cost savings, or AI strategy of any kind. The company lacks the resources and technical capability to develop or deploy AI given its financial distress. Market Share (0/2): Society Pass is a micro-cap participant with negligible market share in the highly competitive Southeast Asian digital economy, where it competes against well-funded platforms like Grab, Shopee, GoTo, and established local players. The 3.3M registered users and 205K merchants represent a small fraction of the region's digital commerce market. Product Pipeline (0/2): No visible product pipeline. The company is in Chapter 11 bankruptcy, and its primary operational focus is survival and restructuring rather than product development [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No evidence of meaningful R&D spending. The company's TTM revenue of $7.1M and net losses of -$10.2M leave no resources for meaningful research and development.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Society Pass's stated purpose as a digital ecosystem connecting consumers and merchants across Southeast Asia is generic — interchangeable with dozens of e-commerce platforms in the region. No distinctive vision or deeper purpose beyond building a digital marketplace was identified. The mission does not articulate why Society Pass exists beyond commercial opportunity. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of charitable giving, community programs, or social impact initiatives. A company with $7.1M in TTM revenue, net losses of $10.2M, and bankruptcy proceedings has no resources to devote to community investment [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): No employee retention data available. The Chapter 11 filing and Nasdaq delisting suggest significant organizational instability that would naturally drive employee departures [1]. The company's small size (~200 employees across 5 countries) makes meaningful retention analysis impossible with available data. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of insider buying. The stock's collapse and bankruptcy filing make open-market purchases unlikely.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: Average daily volume of ~331,000 shares at a stock price of ~$0.37 yields daily dollar volume of approximately $122,000 — well below the $1,000,000 minimum [3]. Infrastructure score is automatically set to 0 regardless of other metrics. Even without the liquidity floor, the metrics are dire: ROE is deeply negative (the company loses $10.2M annually on $7.1M in revenue, a -143% profit margin), revenue declined 18% YoY, forward P/E is unavailable (negative earnings), and the company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2026 [1][2]. The one acceptable metric is low D/E (~7%) with $15.3M cash against $0.8M debt, but this cash is now subject to bankruptcy proceedings.

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Society Pass operates a digital marketing and e-commerce platform — a sector with meaningful AI exposure. AI-powered marketing tools (automated ad creative, personalized targeting, content generation) are rapidly displacing the manual digital marketing services that small platforms like SOPA provide. AI-native e-commerce platforms from major players (Shopee's AI recommendations, Grab's AI-driven services) are widening the competitive gap [2]. However, Society Pass's local merchant relationships and physical-world commerce connections in Southeast Asia provide some protection from purely digital AI disruption. The company's existential threat is not AI — it is financial insolvency — but in a hypothetical recovery scenario, AI disruption would be a material risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue. No AI products. No AI strategy. The company lacks the capital, talent, and technological capability to develop AI-powered offerings.

infinite_game.summary: Society Pass is in pure survival mode. A company in Chapter 11 bankruptcy with Nasdaq delisting proceedings is, by definition, not playing an infinite game — it is fighting for its right to continue existing. No Just Cause, no courageous leadership decisions, no trusting teams, no existential flexibility, and no worthy rival awareness were identified. The company expanded into 5 countries across multiple verticals without achieving product-market fit in any of them, a pattern of finite-game thinking that prioritizes growth metrics over sustainable value creation [1].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): No Just Cause is evident. Society Pass exists to build a digital marketplace in Southeast Asia, which is a commercial objective, not a vision of a future state that inspires sacrifice. The company's multi-country, multi-vertical strategy suggests a growth-at-all-costs mentality rather than a purpose-driven approach. The Chapter 11 filing is the ultimate evidence that the company optimized for expansion over sustainability [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Chapter 11 bankruptcy and Nasdaq delisting destroy organizational trust. Employees face job insecurity, creditors are enforcing claims, and the company's future is uncertain [1]. Operations across 5 countries with ~200 employees suggest a thinly-spread organization with limited capacity for the kind of organizational depth that builds trust. No evidence of employee empowerment, cultural practices, or leadership continuity was identified.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of competitive self-awareness or rival acknowledgment. Society Pass operated in markets dominated by Grab, Shopee, GoTo, and established local players, but there is no evidence the company learned from these rivals' strengths or used competitive pressure to improve its own offerings.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): Society Pass has not demonstrated strategic flexibility. The company maintained its multi-country, multi-vertical digital platform strategy even as revenue declined and losses mounted, suggesting rigidity rather than adaptation [2]. The Chapter 11 filing is a forced restructuring driven by financial distress, not a strategic pivot in service of a higher cause. A company that is too small and too young to have meaningfully tested this dimension.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of courageous leadership decisions. The company expanded aggressively across 5 countries while burning cash, ultimately ending in bankruptcy — this represents reckless optimism rather than the kind of courage Sinek describes [1]. No examples of leadership sacrificing short-term results for long-term capability, investing during downturns, or taking principled stances that cost money were identified.

investment_thesis: There is no bull case for Society Pass at this time. The company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 12, 2026, Nasdaq suspended trading on May 21, 2026, and the stock trades OTC at approximately $0.37 with a market cap near $1M [1]. TTM revenue of $7.1M against net losses of $10.2M demonstrates a business model that does not work — the company burns $1.43 for every $1 in revenue it generates [2][3]. The most recent quarter showed revenue declining 18% YoY, accelerating the negative trajectory. Even the Inspire Impact Score of 33 (ALIGNED) cannot offset the fundamental business failure.
thesis_continued: The risks are existential and immediate. Chapter 11 restructuring may not result in a viable going concern — the company's assets (registered users and merchant relationships across 5 SE Asian countries) have uncertain value in bankruptcy proceedings, and creditor enforcement has been stayed but not eliminated [1]. Nasdaq delisting removes institutional investor access and liquidity, creating a spiral of declining share price and trading volume (daily dollar volume already below $125K). Even if the company emerges from bankruptcy, the competitive landscape in Southeast Asian digital commerce is dominated by Grab, Shopee, and GoTo, all of which have orders-of-magnitude more capital, technology, and market share. The $15.3M cash balance is subject to bankruptcy proceedings and may be consumed by restructuring costs, legal fees, and operating losses before any recovery plan can be executed.
key_catalysts: Successful Chapter 11 restructuring and emergence as a viable going concern — though this is speculative and depends on court approval, creditor agreement, and operational turnaround [1]
Potential strategic acquisition of the company's user base (3.3M registered users) and merchant network (205K) by a larger Southeast Asian digital platform at a premium to current distressed pricing
Nasdaq delisting appeal success — maintaining listing status would preserve institutional access and liquidity, though this appears unlikely given the bankruptcy filing [1]
key_risks: Chapter 11 bankruptcy may result in complete equity wipeout — shareholders are last in line behind secured creditors, unsecured creditors, and preferred holders in a liquidation scenario [1]
Nasdaq delisting eliminates institutional investor access and accelerates the liquidity death spiral — daily dollar volume of ~$125K makes meaningful position building or exiting impossible [3]

Revenue declining 18% YoY while operating at a -143% profit margin demonstrates a fundamentally broken business model with no clear path to profitability even under optimistic restructuring scenarios [2]
